hardy.statement: hardy's theorem: infinitely many nontrivial zeros lie exactly on the critical line — the count of line zeros up to height t tends to infinity as t tends to infinity

li-criterion.statement: the Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if every Li number is positive — the Li number of index n is the derivative of order n minus one, at s = 1, of s to the power n minus one times the log of the completed function, divided by (n minus 1) factorial — and the check up to n = ten to the fifth is a declared numerical fact, not a proof

lindelof.statement: the lindelof hypothesis claims that zeta at one-half plus i t is bounded by a power of t to the epsilon for every epsilon greater than zero; the riemann hypothesis implies lindelof — one direction only: the reverse is not in my store

mean-square.statement: the classical mean square: the integral of the squared modulus of zeta on the critical line from height 0 to t is t times log(t over 2 pi) plus (2 gamma minus 1) times t, with an error of at most a constant times log t

pi-eq.statement: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the fact that the prime-counting function is the logarithmic integral of x plus an error of at most the square root of x times log x

pnt-error.statement: the zero-free region implies the prime number theorem with an explicit error: the chebyshev psi of x is x plus O of x times e to the minus c times the square root of log x, for a constant c greater than zero; the value of the constant is not in my store

polya-hilbert.statement: the polya-hilbert program reformulates the Riemann hypothesis as a spectral statement about a positive self-adjoint operator; the reformulation is a theorem, and the step that recovers the conjecture from the spectrum is an open program, not in my store

psi-eq.statement: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the fact that the chebyshev psi of x is x plus an error of at most x to the one-half plus epsilon, for every epsilon greater than zero

st-eq.statement: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the fact that the argument wiggle S of T is little-o of log T as T tends to infinity

zero-density.statement: the littlewood zero-density bound: the number of zeros with real part at least sigma and height at most T is at most T to the power 3(1 minus sigma) over (2 minus sigma), times a power of log T

zero-free-region.statement: zeta has no zero when the real part of s is at least one minus c over log of the absolute value of t, for a constant c greater than zero — the classical zero-free region; the value of the constant is not in my store

criterion-gap.statement: the best error term in my store, of order x times e to the minus c times the square root of log x, does not meet the scale the equivalence demands, x to the one-half plus epsilon: for every fixed c greater than zero and every epsilon below one-half, the former eventually exceeds the latter, and their ratio grows without bound — the square-root improvement is the missing ingredient

mirror-region.statement: by the reflection symmetry, the zero-free region has a mirror: zeta has no zero when the real part of s is at most c over log of the absolute value of t — the left-side region is the image of the right-side region under the map s to 1 minus s
